The first background run reviewed the wrong diff (a stale `FETCH_HEAD`); the re-run against the correct branch found real issues. Here's the consolidated review.

## Review — Trail 1034: "Simplify CLI login management"

**Branch:** `dip/simplify-login-management` · 44 files, +687/−2441 · `f90ad274e`

**What it does:** collapses the kubectl-style multi-context auth model into a single "current login" stored in the OS keychain (service `entire-login`), removes `auth contexts` / `auth use` / `logout --all-contexts` / context-switching, and adds a one-time migration off `~/.config/entire/contexts.json`. Docs (`CLAUDE.md`, `upstream-host-resolution.md`) are kept in sync, and the refactor is mostly clean mechanical renaming (`context` → `login`) with good new test coverage. Builds clean, auth/contexts/cli suites pass.

The design is sound. My concerns are all concentrated in the **migration path** in `internal/entireclient/contexts/contexts.go`:

### High — token leak + silent logout when legacy `current_context` is empty
`readNoLock` (`contexts.go:~205`): the `current == nil` branch does `os.Remove(legacyPath); return &File{}` and **skips the keychain-cleanup loop** that the `current != nil` branch runs. A legacy `contexts.json` with contexts but no `current_context` is reachable (on `main`, `File.Delete` clears `current_context` without promoting; entiredb also writes the shared file). Result: every stored context's access **and refresh** tokens stay orphaned in the keychain — unaddressable by any future `entire logout`, never revoked server-side — and the user is silently logged out. `TestLoadMigratesOnlyCurrentLegacyContext` only covers the `current != nil` path, so this is untested.

### High — migration deletes the `contexts.json` that entiredb shares
The old package doc stated *"Both CLIs share the same file so a login from either is visible to the other."* Migration unconditionally `os.Remove(legacyPath)` after preserving only `entire`'s one current login. For a user of both `entire` and entiredb, entiredb's other context entries (core URL, handle, keychain-slot pointers) are destroyed on the first post-upgrade `entire` invocation; its cluster tokens survive in the keychain but become unaddressable → entiredb reads as logged out. Worth confirming whether entiredb still shares this file — if so, migration needs to preserve entries it doesn't own.

### Medium — any non-`ErrNotFound` keychain error is now fatal
`readNoLock`: a keychain that's temporarily unavailable or access-denied makes `tokenstore.Get` return a non-`ErrNotFound` error, and `Load` hard-errors (`read login metadata: …`). Previously a missing/unreadable file degraded to "logged out." Now `status`, control-plane resolution, and git/cluster resolution all break on a transient keychain condition. Consider treating unexpected read errors as logged-out, matching prior behavior.

### Medium — `contexts.Load` now hits the keychain on every call
`Load` is on hot paths — git-remote-entire (every fetch/push), the import/hook path, every auth resolution — and now issues a keychain round-trip for the metadata item on top of the existing token read. On some macOS configs that also adds access-prompt surface where before it was a plain local file read.

### Low (verify) — collateral token deletion when two legacy contexts share a keychain slot
The `current != nil` cleanup loop guards only on `old.Name == current.Name`, but the access/refresh delete keys on `(old.KeychainService, old.Handle)`. Two contexts created via `login --name` for the **same account/core** share the same slot with different names; migrating with one as current would delete the *current* login's own tokens. Note the jurisdiction-audience loop just below already guards this case (`old.Handle == current.Handle && currentAudiences[audience]`) — the token delete above it doesn't. Niche, but the asymmetry looks unintended.
